title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
description: Ten verified no-cost ways for Harvey Mudd students to share art, music, study time, archives, and community events in Claremont.

cards.title: Catch a Concert at Drinkward
cards.subtitle: Free public performances at Harvey Mudd
cards.notes: Check the Arts at Harvey Mudd schedule, then meet downstairs in Shanahan; doors open 30 minutes before each listed concert.
cards.short_summary: Gather for a ticketless recital in Harvey Mudd’s 99-seat performance hall.
cards.evidence_claim: Arts at Harvey Mudd states that its concerts are open to the public unless noted, all events are free, and no tickets or reservations are required.
cards.source_title: Visit — Arts at Harvey Mudd College
cards.access_notes: Public unless an event description says otherwise; no ticket or reservation required. The hall opens 30 minutes before concerts and has limited seating.

cards.title: Walk Through Sprague Gallery
cards.subtitle: No-cost visual art inside Shanahan Center
cards.notes: Drop in with a friend on a weekday, compare one work each, and consult the event listing before relying on evening or weekend access.
cards.short_summary: Turn a campus break into a shared look at Harvey Mudd’s current visual-art display.
cards.evidence_claim: Arts at Harvey Mudd says exhibitions are publicly accessible unless noted, all events are free, and Sprague Gallery is normally open Monday through Friday from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.
cards.source_title: Visit — Arts at Harvey Mudd College
cards.access_notes: Open Monday–Friday, 8 a.m.–5 p.m., with additional event hours; confirm that an exhibition is installed before visiting.

cards.title: Browse a Library Exhibit Together
cards.subtitle: Public displays at Honnold/Mudd Library
cards.notes: Choose a current exhibition from the library page, bring photo ID for check-in, and walk the display together without applying for a card.
cards.short_summary: Explore a rotating library exhibition without borrowing anything or buying admission.
cards.evidence_claim: The Claremont Colleges Library welcomes visitors to explore exhibits, says no Community Card is required for general exhibit visitors, and requires desk check-in with photo ID.
cards.source_title: Visitor Access – The Claremont Colleges Library
cards.access_notes: Harvey Mudd students may use their college access; general visitors must check in with valid photo ID. Public availability can vary by exhibit.

cards.entity_name: The Claremont Colleges Library Open Study Spaces
cards.title: Hold a No-Spend Study Meetup
cards.subtitle: Open study space for the Claremont Colleges
cards.notes: Pick an open table, set a shared work interval, and use campus connectivity; visitors should review check-in and blackout restrictions first.
cards.short_summary: Share focused study time in the consortium library’s open spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: The library identifies students of The Claremont Colleges as its primary users and describes open study spaces and free limited guest Wi-Fi for eligible visitors.
cards.source_title: Visitor Access – The Claremont Colleges Library
cards.access_notes: Harvey Mudd students should bring college identification. Visitor access and Community Access Cards may be limited by eligibility and finals blackout dates.

cards.entity_name: The Claremont Colleges Special Collections and Archives
cards.title: Examine Archives by Appointment
cards.subtitle: A no-cost encounter with rare materials
cards.notes: Choose a collection topic, contact the archives before your visit, and request a small set of materials that your group can examine together.
cards.short_summary: Plan a social research session around rare books, archives, or artifacts.
cards.evidence_claim: The library states that Special Collections and Archives are open to everyone at no cost, with in-person visits available by appointment.
cards.source_title: Visitor Access – The Claremont Colleges Library
cards.access_notes: Advance appointment required; contact Special Collections and Archives to request materials and arrange the visit.

cards.title: See an Exhibition at Williamson Gallery
cards.subtitle: Free public art at neighboring Scripps College
cards.notes: Walk over during an exhibition, meet in the Eleventh Street courtyard, and give everyone time to select one object for group discussion.
cards.short_summary: Visit a named neighboring gallery for a relaxed, purchase-free art outing.
cards.evidence_claim: The Ruth Chandler Williamson Gallery’s official visitor page states that admission is free and the gallery is open to the public during exhibitions.
cards.access_notes: Open during exhibitions Wednesday–Sunday, noon–5 p.m.; confirm exhibition dates before walking over. Donations are optional.

cards.entity_name: Benton Museum of Art at Pomona College
cards.title: Meet Up at the Benton Museum
cards.subtitle: Free exhibitions on the Pomona campus edge
cards.notes: Check the current exhibition list, meet by the museum courtyard, and explore at your own pace before regrouping around a chosen artwork.
cards.short_summary: Build a neighboring-campus hang around contemporary and historic art.
cards.evidence_claim: The Benton Museum’s official support page says the museum remains free and open to all.
cards.access_notes: Open to all without admission charge; consult the museum’s Visit and Exhibitions pages for current operating hours and installation changes.

cards.title: Bring a Blanket to a Monday Concert
cards.subtitle: Free summer music at Memorial Park
cards.notes: Meet on the Memorial Park lawn before 7 p.m., bring your own blanket and water, and enjoy the performance without purchasing concessions.
cards.short_summary: Share an outdoor concert while the city’s 2026 series is still running.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Claremont announced a free eight-week concert series at Memorial Park every Monday from July 6 through August 24, 2026, from 7 to 8:30 p.m.
cards.source_title: City of Claremont’s Monday Night Concert Series
cards.access_notes: Remaining 2026 concerts are scheduled for August 17 and August 24, 7–8:30 p.m., at Memorial Park. Food sales are optional.

cards.title: Dance at the Fall Ball
cards.subtitle: An inclusive free event at the Youth Activity Center
cards.notes: Eligible students can register with family, choose the age-appropriate session, and plan to keep the required parent or guardian on site.
cards.short_summary: Join a structured, no-cost dance designed for people with special needs and their families.
cards.evidence_claim: Claremont’s official inclusion-events page lists the September 18, 2026 Fall Ball as a free event for people with special needs and their families.
cards.source_title: Special Needs and Inclusion Events | City of Claremont
cards.access_notes: September 18, 2026; ages 5–12 from 6–7 p.m. and ages 13+ from 7–9 p.m. A parent or guardian must attend; registration is required.

cards.title: Join the Halloween Spooktacular
cards.subtitle: Free activities and a sensory zone at Lewis Park
cards.notes: Coordinate costumes with friends, arrive during the afternoon window, and use the sensory zone if anyone in the group needs a quieter option.
cards.short_summary: Celebrate Halloween outdoors with free community activities and inclusive space.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Claremont lists the October 17, 2026 Halloween Spooktacular at Lewis Park as a free event with activities and a sensory zone.
cards.source_title: Special Needs and Inclusion Events | City of Claremont
cards.access_notes: Scheduled for October 17, 2026, from 3–6 p.m. at Lewis Park. Review the linked event details for any updated participation instructions.
